mgmt_bio.text: Brad Jacobs is the founder, chairman and chief executive officer of QXO, Inc., and has founded eight billion-dollar or multibillion-dollar companies, including six publicly traded ones: United Waste Systems, United Rentals, XPO, GXO Logistics, RXO and QXO. Over his career, Jacobs and his teams have completed roughly 500 mergers and acquisitions and raised more than $60 billion in institutional capital. He founded United Waste Systems in 1989 and led it as chairman and CEO for eight years, founded United Rentals in 1997, and led XPO Logistics as chairman and CEO until 2022. He became QXO's chairman and CEO upon the June 6, 2024 closing of a $1 billion equity investment, which took QXO into the roughly $800 billion building products distribution industry.

sentences.quote: The company plans to become the tech-enabled leader in the $800 billion building products distribution industry and generate outsized value for shareholders. QXO is targeting $50 billion in annual revenues within the next decade through accretive acquisitions and organic growth.
sentences.text: QXO is pursuing a roll-up of building products distribution under Brad Jacobs, targeting leadership in the roughly $800 billion industry and annual revenue of $50 billion within the coming decade through accretive acquisitions and organic growth.

The April 2025 purchase of Beacon Roofing Supply for about $11 billion, valued at $10.6 billion at closing and renamed QXO Building Products, gives it nearly 600 branches across the United States and Canada.

Further consolidation is the stated plan, since management believes about 30% of roofing supply remains fragmented among over 500 local dealers, with M&A opportunities in insulation, siding and waterproofing.

The agreed roughly $17 billion acquisition of TopBuild, the largest North American insulation distributor and installer, would make QXO the second largest publicly traded building products distributor in North America.
